messages:
Sam Chen: Heads-up — during last night's canary we saw ~2s extra tail latency for tenants that got routed to the secondary region during a cross-region burst. Looks like cold KV cache + model cold-start overlap. Thinking about a lightweight 'priming handshake' that does async prewarm + bounded write buffering before the flip. Opinions?
Maria Torres: I saw the spikes too. Most pronounced for long-context gen (>=4k). Not sure stalling writes is acceptable for all customers though. :thinking_face:
Cheng Wu: FWIW we can do read-path priming only + short write-buffer replay. Sketch: 1) proxy marks tenant `priming`, routes reads to primary for hot prefixes; 2) background workers populate local KV cache + trigger model prewarm; 3) once ready, proxy swaps traffic and replays buffered writes (idempotent apply). That keeps tail latency down without long global stalls.
Elaine Park: main concern: buffering writes outside resident region violates data residency. We can't persist unencrypted PII in a different region even briefly. If buffer lands in non-resident region we need to encrypt with customer KMS and/or mirror buffer to resident store before swap.
Sam Chen: good point. Implementation note: keep in-memory ephemeral buffer in target region for <10s, but mirror metadata + encrypted payload to resident S3 if tenant residency != target region. Use a `lease-token` to prevent double-apply on replay.
Cheng Wu: sample lease token metadata (for discussion):
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "lease": "priming-v2",
  "expires_at": 1740002000,
  "origin_region": "eu-west-1",
  "sealed": true
}
```
Sam Chen: behavior contract: when proxy sets `priming` state it returns a 202 for new writes with `Retry-After` header (very short) and appends to local buffer. On success we return 200 after replay. If priming fails or lease expires, proxy must return 409 and surface rollback. Keep timeouts tight: default max buffer window = 10s.
Maria Torres: metrics we should track: `priming.buffer_depth`, `priming.duration_ms`, `priming.replay_fail_rate`, `residency.buffer_mirror_rate`. Also add alert if buffer > 1k ops or >10s.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: `proxy/priming-feature` canary -> infra-qa @ 2025-04-08T02:00Z (note: automated smoke will run).
Sam Chen: plan: I'll prototype a minimal flag in proxy (no persistence except mirrored encrypted payloads when needed) and a worker that replays idempotently. Canaries at 5% traffic with opt-out. @Elaine Park can you review residency edge cases?
Elaine Park: happy to. Quick decision point: if priming can't mirror to resident store (network error), do we: a) abort priming and keep routing to old region, b) fallback to synchronous write to resident region (latency hit), or c) accept temporary non-compliance (no). My vote: a) abort and rollback; we must not risk residency.
Cheng Wu: agree with abort. Also add a fast-kill feature: if replay error rate > 0.5% for 30s trigger immediate rollback.
Maria Torres: +1 on kill-switch. Also suggest a low-impact fallback for read-only workloads where we can serve degraded reads instead of blocking writes.
Sam Chen: thanks — I'll iterate on prototype and share a short RFC with sequence diagrams + config knobs (`priming.enabled`, `priming.max_window_s`, `priming.mirror_policy`). Targeting a PR + canary next week.
Elaine Park: I'll review RFC for residency compliance and KMS flow. If we need a quick PoC for encrypted mirror, I can help with integration tests.
Sam Chen: awesome. tagging follow-ups: #priming-rfc, will post link once draft is ready. End of thread.
